title: How to make a background event continue to move during another event?

posts.author: Madre_Joshua
posts.body:
I am currently trying to make a cutscene in which one character is watching television. For this, I have made a special television animation and an event that displays said animation. This event has the following custom movement route.
The intention here is that the character on the television is moving around, with each frame of animation changing every 30 frames, as to not make it look too rapid, like it does if I simply turn the "stepping" animation on. This is the TV in question.
Now, the issue I have is that, while the cutscene plays, the television program ceases to move; The story event is occuring, during which characters talk and move around, but throughout its entire playtime, the television event that's meant to passively cycle through its animations, pauses until the story event is over. How do I prevent the television event from ceasing to move while the story event is occurring?
While one may say "simply turn the story event and the tv event into one, so that the TV is autorunning the cutscene" while something along those lines may be possible, I do want to also just know how to do this in general for future reference, especially when I have multiple events happening during a cutscene that are meant to keep moving, since this solution obviously would not work in taht scenario.
Thank you very much for any possible advice.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
while you have found a solution, the mistake in your original event was a different one.
you should have added an "wait(1)" after the plugin command.
Background:
The main game loop processes one event after another, and unless said event is a parallel process that means completing any command sequence before going to the next event.
However due to the way waits work internally, they are also breaking command sequences up and allow the game loop to process the other events at that time.
your TV event simply has no time to switch to the second page after the plugin command, and you'll need to give that time with a wait - even a short one should be enough
